content.what_it_is: MATLAB function `tight_subplot` (L1) creates an Nh-by-Nw grid of normalized axes. It installs omitted-argument defaults (L29-L31), expands scalar gap and margin arguments to two elements (L33-L41), derives common axes height/width and the first vertical coordinate (L43-L46), creates axes row-wise from the upper left in nested loops (L50-L61), optionally returns their positions (L63-L65), and forces the handle array to a column (L66).
entities: function tight_subplot with outputs ha,pos and inputs Nh,Nw,gap,marg_h,marg_w @L1

equations.ref: normalized axes height after margins and inter-row gaps
normalized axes width after margins and inter-column gaps

unresolved: Explicitly empty `gap` is not treated like an omitted argument: L29 only tests `nargin<3`, L33 skips expansion because numel([])=0, and L43-L44 then index gap(1:2), causing an indexing failure. `marg_h` has an explicit empty check at L30, showing the interface handling is inconsistent.

Explicitly empty `marg_w` likewise bypasses the L31 default and L36 expansion, then L44/L51 index an empty array; the fifth-argument interface therefore fails for `[]` although the fourth argument accepts it.

No validation constrains Nh/Nw to positive integers or two-element vector arguments to exactly two entries (L33-L44); zero dimensions can divide by zero and longer vectors affect sum(marg_*) while only the first two elements are used for placement.
